chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Sukayn and others, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

It was said to him: So-and-so was afflicted with janabah while he had smallpox, so they gave him ghusl and he died. He said: “They killed him. Why did they not ask? Why did they not perform tayammum for him? Indeed, the cure for ignorance is asking.”
He said: And that has also been narrated regarding the one with a fracture and the one suffering from abdominal illness: “He performs tayammum and does not perform ghusl.”

key_terms.الْعِيِّ: inability arising from ignorance or lack of knowing what to do
key_terms.الْكَسِيرِ: the person with a fracture or broken limb
key_terms.الْمَبْطُونِ: the person afflicted with abdominal illness
key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.يَمَّمُوهُ: they should have performed tayammum for him

ai.seo_question: When should a sick person perform tayammum instead of ghusl in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that when using water would seriously harm a person in a state requiring ghusl, tayammum is to be performed instead. It also emphasizes the duty of asking those with knowledge before acting in religious matters, especially when lives and bodily safety are at stake.
